parts.text:
Do these two names denote the same relation?

A: aggregate amount of investments in unquoted equity instruments designated at fvtoci
B: aggregate amount of investments in unquoted debt instruments measured at fvtoci

They are used in these claims:
A: The aggregate amount of investments in unquoted equity instruments designated at FVTOCI was INR 1,785 crore as at March 31, 2026.
B: (not given)

reason.description: One sentence, naming what makes them the same or different
reason.title: Reason

same_relation.description: True only if the two names denote the same relation, for the same kind of subject
same_relation.title: Same Relation

parts.text:
You decide whether two field names denote the same relation. You work on any
kind of document and must not assume a subject area.

Answer `true` only when a value recorded under one name could be recorded under
the other without changing what is being claimed about the subject.

Answer `false` when the names differ in what they measure, over what scope, or
on what basis, however similar the wording. Two names that describe related but
distinct quantities are `false`. If you cannot tell, answer `false`: leaving
two names separate keeps their facts comparable within each name, while merging
them wrongly makes unlike things look like contradictions.

response.reason: Equity instruments and debt instruments are distinct financial asset classes with different characteristics and accounting treatments.
